fields.meta_title: Chiropractic Intake Form for New Patients | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a chiropractic intake form new patients finish before the first exam, with a body pain chart, accident details, and consent. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Chiropractic Intake Form That Maps Pain Before the Exam
fields.hero_description: Build a chiropractic intake form where new patients mark the pain on a body chart, saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Where It Hurts, How It Started, Who Sees It
fields.features_subheading: A chiropractic intake form that records pain the way the exam uses it: where it is, how bad it gets, and what sets it off.
fields.feature_1:
A body chart patients tap, front and back

New patients tap each spot that hurts on a front and back body chart, then rate each one from 0 to 10. The chiropractor opens the intake to a marked map instead of a blank line.
fields.feature_2:
When it started, and what makes it worse

Ask when the pain began and what the patient was doing at the time. A second question asks what makes it worse, with sitting and bending as choices and a box for anything else.
fields.feature_3:
Car accident questions that open on a yes

Patients hurt in a car accident get their own branch: when it happened, who insures the car, the claim on file, and any attorney. Those cases go to whoever handles them.
fields.feature_4:
Insurance card photos read into fields

Patients photograph the front of their insurance card, and the app reads the member ID and group number into the intake. A field it cannot read clearly goes to the front desk.
fields.feature_5:
Consent to care signed on the phone

The last screen holds the consent to care. The app captures the patient's signature with the time it was signed, and the front desk sees any first visit still waiting on one.
fields.feature_6:
A codebase the clinic can take with it

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host the intake beside the clinic's own website. A developer can keep building on it from that repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Reads the Intake, and When
fields.tab_content_1:
The pain map Dr. Raleigh reads before 9:15

Larchmont Chiropractic sends the intake with each booking. Gideon Haas taps his lower back and right hip on the body chart and rates the back at 7 of 10. It started 3 weeks ago while moving a couch and gets worse after 30 minutes of sitting. Dr. Imogen Raleigh gets the answers on an email card before his 9:15 exam.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every car accident case reaches Wendell by email

Elodie Marsh was rear-ended on Oct 28 and booked a first visit at Sorrel Ridge Chiropractic. Her yes to the car accident question opens four more: the accident date, her auto insurer, the claim number, and her attorney. The intake goes by email to case coordinator Wendell Kim instead of the health plan queue.
fields.tab_content_3:
From a phone signature to the 9:30 adjustment

The last screen of the Bellmoor Chiropractic intake is its consent to care. Lucan Pryor reads it on his phone and signs with a finger at 8:52, and the app saves the signature with the time. Front desk lead Amara Quist sees Consent signed beside his 9:30 first adjustment. Nobody hands him a clipboard at the counter.
fields.tab_content_4:
By visit 12, neck pain is a 3, down from 8 at intake

Twelve visits in, Quarry Hill Chiropractic sends Celeste Ambrose the pain questions from her intake again. She rates her neck at 3 of 10, against 8 at intake. Sitting at her desk now lasts 45 minutes before it hurts, up from 15. Dr. Priya Duggal sees both sets of answers side by side at the re-exam.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Chiropractic Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a chiropractic intake form around the first exam, then build it with Emergent and test it with a fake patient.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what the first exam needs
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick one pain scale and keep it
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the consent on the last screen
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask each chiropractor in the clinic what they want to know before a new patient walks in. Every question on the form should trace back to a line on that list. A question that traces to nothing comes out, however standard it looks.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use the same 0 to 10 rating on the intake, at every re-exam, and in the exam room. One scale lets a later visit compare cleanly with the first. Leave one free text box for the patient's own words about the pain.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name the person who takes car accident cases, plus a backup for their days off. Then list what that person needs on the first day, such as the claim number, and make those questions required only after a yes.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the clinic's own consent to care, in its current wording, into the final screen. Patients sign with a finger before they submit. When the wording changes, keep the old version with the consents signed under it.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the questions and the consent wording into one prompt. Emergent builds the chiropractic intake form, the database behind it, and a screen for the front desk. Change a question later by asking for it in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send the link with the booking
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add the intake link to the booking confirmation email, so patients answer at home instead of in the waiting room. Ask for a photo of the insurance card in the same pass, and send one email reminder the day before the first visit.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book a made-up new patient, fill in the intake on a phone, and report a car accident as the cause. Check that the case coordinator gets the email, the consent shows as signed, and the pain answers land in the patient record.

faq_plan.q: What is a chiropractic intake form?
faq_plan.a: A chiropractic intake form is the set of questions a new patient answers before the first chiropractic visit. It tells the chiropractor where the pain is and how it began, and it gives the front desk the contact and insurance details it needs, plus a signed consent.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a chiropractic intake form?
faq_plan.a: List what the first exam needs, decide who handles car accident cases, and settle the consent wording. Then describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form patients fill in on their phones and the database where each intake lands.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a chiropractic intake form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with where it hurts on a body chart and a 0 to 10 rating for each spot. Follow with when the pain started, what the patient was doing, and what makes it worse. Then ask whether a car accident caused it, collect contact and insurance details, and close with the consent to care.

faq_plan.q: Can a chiropractic intake form also cover massage appointments?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with a branch that opens only when the booking includes massage. Ask those patients about pressure and any areas to avoid, questions the chiropractic exam does not use. If the clinic books massage on its own, send a separate massage intake form and keep both sets of answers on one patient record.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a chiropractic intake form easy to finish on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Show one question per screen and make the body chart something patients tap rather than draw on. Put the required questions first and the optional ones after them. Emergent can build the intake as a conversational flow, one question per screen, from the same prompt.

faq_plan.q: Who should see the answers on a chiropractic intake form?
faq_plan.a: Only the people who act on them. Give the chiropractor the pain answers, the front desk the insurance and consent status, and the case coordinator the car accident details. Ask for a separate screen for each of those roles when you describe the form.

faq_plan.q: Can a family member fill out a chiropractic intake form for a patient?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a question that asks who is filling in the form and how they are related to the patient, and keep the patient's own name and date of birth as separate fields. If the patient also gets care at home, ask for the agency's name; that agency keeps its own home care intake form.

faq_plan.q: How long should a chiropractic intake form take to fill out?
faq_plan.a: Aim for one sitting of about 10 minutes on a phone. Ask only what the first exam and the front desk will use, and leave the rest for the chiropractor to ask in the exam room. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Can chiropractic intake forms read an insurance card photo?
faq_plan.a: Yes. From a photo of the card's front, the app pulls the plan name, member ID, and group number onto the patient record. Any value it reads with low confidence goes to a person at the front desk to confirm before the visit.

faq_plan.q: Should a chiropractic intake form ask about stress?
faq_plan.a: Ask one plain, optional question about stress at work or at home if the chiropractor uses the answer when planning care. Anything deeper about mood or mental health belongs on a therapy intake form from a licensed counselor, not on the chiropractic intake.
